title: Telemetry Garden — Standup & Weekly Lab Notes (2026-10-22)
content:
Context and purpose:
This is the standup capture and lab notebook for the 'Telemetry Garden' initiative — our week-focused, experimental playbook for trimming trace ingestion cost while keeping actionable spans for debugging. Notes are intentionally candid: experiments, rough metrics, owner decisions, and unresolved questions.

Summary bullets:
- Small wins: preliminary sampling adjustments yielded an ~18% drop in trace ingestion cost in eu-west-1 (night window).
- Dashboard work: three large widget queries refactored to use pre-aggregated metrics; dashboard load 95th percentile improved by ~30ms.
- Short-term risk: reduced sampling uncovered a rare encoding bug in the internal span schema (OBS-4823) that causes a missing field in long-tail traces.

Standup highlights (2026-10-22):
- Priya: ran the adaptive-sampling A/B for 24h on the qa-lab cluster; cost numbers look good but need validation for SLO regressions. Next: extend to two customer-sim clusters (canary).
- Evan: dashboard refactor PR split into incremental commits: query rewrite, materialized view add, and UX tweak. QA flagged a confusing label on model-version selector (UX ticket attached).
- Samira: traced and filed OBS-4823 for missing span attribute (stack frame truncated in p50+ traces). Tentative root cause: older agent version reserializes tags differently when payload > 12KB.
- Liam: started runbook draft for sampling rollback and emergency re-ingestion. Need approvals from SRE and Platform.

Data & quick metrics (night window 02:00-05:00 UTC):
- Trace ingest bytes (eu-west-1): baseline week before = 1.12 TB nightly; after adaptive-sampling = 0.92 TB nightly (-17.9%).
- Span count ingested: baseline = 340M spans; after = 280M spans (-17.6%).
- Ingest cost delta: estimated saving ~$1.9k/day across eu-west region (needs finance validation).
- Dashboard render p95 for "service-overview" widget: baseline = 420ms, after = 390ms (improvement 30ms).
- Error budget impact: no alerts triggered in first 24h for critical pipelines; still monitoring trace-derived SLOs.

Experiments: adaptive-sampling A/B details
- Hypothesis: applying service-priority sampling with a small retention multiplier for low-priority services will reduce ingest by ~15-25% without affecting oncall-runbook success rate.
- Configuration: weight multiplier = 0.4 for low-priority, 1.0 for high-priority; prefix caching enabled for hot paths.
- Buckets: control (no sampling change) vs experiment (adaptive) across 10% of traffic to qa-lab then 20% to canary.
- Observations: certain background jobs (data-ingest-worker) have extremely chatty spans that are low-value — these dropped dramatically under sample 0.4. However, one customer pipeline (cust-24) reported missing a correlation id in traces (likely agent version mismatch).

Dashboard maintenance notes:
- Widgets refactored to rely on aggregated 'span_counts_by_pri' materialized view (PR #718). This removed two JOINs per query and reduced read cost by ~12% for the dashboard dataset.
- Action: schedule a one-hour dashboard maintenance window to reorder heavy widgets (owner: Evan; ETA: 2026-10-25). Add banner to console when we flip the materialized view refresh to every 60s.
- TODO: annotate dashboards with the sampling policy in effect per environment (dev/staging/prod) so users know why numbers differ.

Runbook and operationalization:
- Liam started a "Sampling rollback" runbook with all steps, checks, and emergency SLAs. Key steps: toggle-policy -> verify ingest -> compare p95 dashboard load -> run ingestion sanity query.
- Need a short script to rehydrate a sampled span set for debugging (replay ingestion). Ticket JIRA-OBS-4999 created (owner: Liam).
- Decision: Rollback can be initiated by oncall + SRE lead; automated rollback only after 3 consecutive failed health checks (thresholds TBD).

Blockers & risks:
- OBS-4823 (missing span field) blocks wider rollout; currently affects ~0.4% of traces but is concentrated in long-running jobs — may bias RCA.
- Materialized view scheduling requires infra quota update for the analytics cluster. Platform team engagement needed (PR sent).
- Need a small HSM integration for secure storage of certain correlation metadata before re-ingestion (compliance ask).

Action items and owners (short list):
- Priya: expand adaptive A/B to canary clusters (target 2026-10-24). Check for SLO regressions 48h post-rollout.
- Evan: deploy PR #718 to staging and schedule maintenance banner (target 2026-10-25).
- Samira: finish reproduction for OBS-4823 and test this against agent v1.4 and v1.5 (deadline 2026-10-23).
- Liam: finish runbook and the rehydration script prototype; attach to JIRA-OBS-4999 (deadline 2026-10-27).
- Priya + Finance: validate ingest cost saving numbers and compute monthlyized estimate (deadline 2026-10-28).

Notes to self (rough/jot):
- If we widen sample multiplier to 0.3 we might save another ~6-8% but QA coverage needs to measure tail debugging success rate.
- Consider a "sample-on-error" tag: always retain traces that contain error-level spans regardless of sampling bucket. (Would help oncall).
- Investigate correlating sample decisions with request latencies; might identify mis-sampled hot requests.

Open questions for next sync:
- What are acceptable thresholds for 'debuggability' loss? (need input from SEs and a few high-volume customers)
- Can platform support materialized view refresh every 30s in eu-west if we need faster dashboards?
- What's the rollback SLA window that legal/compliance is comfortable with for rehydration workflows?

Meeting artifacts & references:
- Experimental config (qa-lab): /repos/observability/configs/telemetry-garden/adaptive-sample.yaml (see PR #718)
- Runbook draft: Confluence (link in linked_artifacts)
- Slack thread: #obs-telemetry-garden — key decision at 10:15AM: proceed to canary if OBS-4823 repro fixed.

Next sync: 2026-10-25, 09:30 PDT — focused on canary rollout decision and OBS-4823 repro status.

-- end of notes --

(Handwritten-ish closing: keep experimenting but keep emergency rollback button obvious; prioritize developer debuggability over marginal cost wins.)
